card.name: Subject noun just before a warning verb
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject phrase (a drug name, therapy, agent or pages) or a linking word right after it, where a caution or risk statement is about to follow. Seen in warning and precaution text.

modes.label: Drug name then may
modes.description: A drug name ends the subject and 'may' follows, leading into a warned effect.
modes.example: Use of ketorolac tromethamine<< may>> blunt the CV effects of several therapeutic agents

modes.label: Subject noun before a predicate
modes.description: A noun such as therapy, clearing, agent or pages ends a subject just before a statement of harm or need.
modes.example: However, even short-term<< therapy>> is not without risk.

modes.label: Comma or and after a drug phrase
modes.description: A comma or 'and' follows a drug or benefit phrase, before a restriction or added risk.
